card.profile: Awki awki is a folk dance performed in the La Paz Department of Bolivia and the Huancané Province of Peru. Derived from the Aymara word auqui, meaning father or old man with a reduplication indicating a collective noun, the dance satirizes elderly Spanish conquerors of the colonial period. Performers wear formal colonial suits, large woven straw hats, and masks with long white beards.
card.insight: In Awki awki, men don masks with long white beards and large woven straw hats to satirize the elderly Spanish conquerors of the colonial period.

card.profile_long: Awki awki, also known as Auqui Auqui, is a traditional folk dance documented in the La Paz Department of Bolivia and the Huancané Province of Peru. The name originates from the Aymara word auqui, which translates to father or old man. The term features a reduplication that forms a collective noun, indicating a group of such figures. Culturally and historically, the dance serves as a form of satire directed at the elderly Spanish conquerors of the colonial period. In terms of performance and attire, the dance is executed exclusively by men. Participants wear distinct costumes that represent formal colonial-era suits. Their physical presentation is enhanced by large hats made of woven straw and detailed masks that depict elderly men characterized by long white beards. Beyond these core descriptive elements derived from foundational records, detailed accounts regarding specific choreography, musical accompaniment, footwork patterns, instrumentation, and performance occasions remain largely unrecorded in current documentation.

observation.setting: Indoor stage with a wooden floor, dark curtains, and illuminated vertical white drapes in the background under changing red and blue stage lights.
observation.dancers: A group of approximately 14-16 dancers, mixed group, appearing to be adults.
observation.formation_and_space: Dancers start in low crouched positions scattered across the stage, then transition into a diagonal line formation, and later form a circle, shifting positions while maintaining synchronized movement.
observation.posture: Heavily bent knees with torsos leaning forward or crouched low, maintaining a deep squat or low stance throughout most of the movement.
observation.footwork: Stepping and shifting weight in a low squat or crouching posture; fast rhythmic footwork and stomping cannot be clearly detailed due to wide stage framing and low angle.
observation.arms_and_hands: Arms held out to the sides or holding walking sticks/canes in one hand and white cloths in the other, moving rhythmically with the dance.
observation.hips_and_torso: Torsos leaned forward with slight upper body shaking or bouncing in rhythm with the music, remaining in a low posture.
observation.partnering: None; dancers perform in a group ensemble without physical contact between partners.
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Low level maintained in deep crouches and squats; small turns and circular group rotations while staying low.
observation.costume_and_props: Traditional-style folkloric costumes with colorful patterned trousers (blue, red, green), patterned vests or jackets, wide-brimmed hats with white decorations or veils covering the face, holding walking sticks and white cloths.
observation.cannot_infer: Exact footwork details, weight transfer nuances, and facial expressions are obscured by distance and low lighting.

signature_moments.what: Dancers transition from a scattered low crouch into a diagonal line while maintaining deep knee bends and shaking upper bodies.
Dancers in a low crouch form a circle, shuffling and rotating in unison while waving white cloths and holding sticks.
